Her talk examines how authenticity, transparency, and meaningful relationships shape public perception and influence. She highlights why genuine connections and consistent communication matter more than mere visibility, encouraging audiences to build trust and use their influence responsibly. Vaishnavi Bhupalam is the Founder of Kinfluence Media, a seven-figure marketing agency that helps founders build influential personal brands and enables businesses to scale through influencer marketing. Her entrepreneurial journey began after facing hundreds of rejections, an experience that taught her to stop waiting for opportunities and start creating them. description: What if the health of a community could be measured not just by statistics, but by its stories, its creativity, and the walls that surround us? After nearly three decades painting murals in neighborhoods across America, Leon Rainbow has discovered that public art is more than decoration—it reveals a community’s pulse. Through powerful stories of transformation, recovery, and collaboration, he invites us to see walls not as barriers, but as mirrors reflecting who we are and who we can become. This talk will challenge audiences to recognize creativity as a vital sign of thriving communities and inspire them to become active participants in shaping the places they call home. Leon Rainbow is a nationally recognized muralist, public artist, educator, and founder of Jersey Fresh Jam, one of New Jersey’s longest-running celebrations of hip-hop culture. For more than 25 years, he has transformed schools, neighborhoods, parks, recovery centers, and public spaces into vibrant works of art that
title: What walls teach us about human connection | Leon Rainbow | TEDxCapeMay

description:
Singing is a joyful, human activity. It can also be incredibly vulnerable. Jessica Gallagher-Steuver, conductor of Windsong, Cleveland's Feminist Chorus, will highlight the unique sense of belonging that can come from group singing in a radically affirming environment. Jessica L. Gallagher-Steuver is a music educator, choral conductor, performer and clinician. She is a visiting assistant professor of music education at Baldwin Wallace Conservatory and has taught at Cleveland State University and Case Western Reserve University.

Gallagher-Steuver is artistic director of Windsong, Cleveland's feminist chorus, a nonprofit organization focused on music and social justice. In 2025, she founded the  Journal of Queer Choral Studies, the official academic publication of GALA Choruses. Her research focuses on queer studies in music education, the social and emotional benefits of choral singing, vocal health in older adults and community music-making. One person. One action. One small moment that you might forget— but someone else never does. I used to think making an impact meant doing something big. Something people would notice. But one day, something very small changed the way I saw it.

Saurabh Gupta, Co-Founder of FROGO, explores why human qualities remain invaluable in an increasingly automated and AI-driven world. His talk highlights the importance of empathy, creativity, emotional intelligence, critical thinking, and human connection in shaping the future. He encourages audiences to embrace technological progress while recognising that our ability to understand, connect with, and care for others remains one of humanity’s greatest strengths. Saurabh Gupta is a technology entrepreneur, author, speaker, and product leader with over two decades of experience across psychology, artificial intelligence, data analytics, and business transformation. An alumnus of Harvard Business School and BITS Pilani, he began his journey as a psychology practitioner before moving into technology leadership roles at Oracle, GE, and Michelin.

Her talk encourages audiences to recognise the importance of protecting urban lakes, preserving natural ecosystems, and taking collective responsibility for building a sustainable future. Revathi Kamath is an environmentalist, entrepreneur, philanthropist, landscaper, and accomplished Veena musician dedicated to creating meaningful social and environmental impact. Her work spans education, healthcare, environmental conservation, social welfare, and sustainable development. With a deep commitment to service, she has worked towards improving lives and supporting communities, particularly those in need. Driven by a deep commitment to animal conservation, she explores ethical, viable alternatives to conventional animal leather, investigating how material innovation and cruelty-free alternatives can reshape everyday industries. An avid reader of non-fiction and a passionate singer, Sahithi combines analytical curiosity with empathy-driven activism. Grounded in the conviction that sustainable transformation begins with personal responsibility, she uses her platform to advocate for conscious consumer choices and compassionate environmental solutions. Sahana Sivanesan is a Grade 9 student and observant cultural thinker dedicated to deconstructing societal norms, media narratives, and everyday assumptions. Focused on adolescent identity and mental wellness, she examines how conventional beauty standards shape teenage self-perception, advocating for a healthier, more authentic dialogue around self-worth. Sahana channels her reflective approach through creative mediums such as drawing and dance, using artistic expression to communicate nuanced ideas. Passionate about asking the uncomfortable questions that spark necessary conversations, she empowers her peers to look beyond outward expectations and cultivate independent critical thought. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community.

Her vision inspires us to reconnect with nature and reimagine cities as sustainable spaces that can breathe. Riya T A is a 13-year-old student and emerging climate advocate interested in ecological innovation and sustainable infrastructure. Driven by a keen curiosity about environmental science, she explores how bio-inspired technologies—such as cellulosic leaves—can be woven into modern urban architecture to actively combat carbon emissions. Known for her articulate stage presence and methodical approach to collaborative problem-solving, Riya balances her scientific inquiries with a passion for singing, dance, and cultural discovery. She aims to inspire fellow young thinkers to reimagine urban spaces through the dual lenses of ecological stewardship and creative engineering. I once asked some of my classmates: “Do you have any role models?” Their answers varied. Some saw themselves as their own role model, some saw their parents as theirs, and some didn’t have any at all. Older people, celebrities—everyone can be a role model. Mine is my mum. Seeing her juggle so many responsibilities under pressure and do everything so well makes me realize what a strong person she is.
 Ayska is a student at Cahaya Rancamaya High School in Indonesia. She has been interested in reading and writing since she was a child, and is now exploring the world of public speaking.  Sharing opinions and ideas—such as in group work and discussion sessions that encourage people to share their perspectives—has always been one of her favorite activities. By participating in TEDx, she hopes to inspire others and learn from them as well. description: ¿Cuáles son las decisiones fundamentales que definen el rumbo de nuestra existencia y nos permiten conectar con nuestro verdadero propósito?   En esta profunda charla compartida en TEDxToluca, el académico y conferencista internacional Dr. Chandra Choubey profundiza en la naturaleza humana, la mente y el poder transformador de nuestras elecciones cotidianas. Con una trayectoria de más de dos décadas dedicadas a la educación superior y el desarrollo del talento humano, el Dr. Choubey reflexiona sobre cómo el autoconocimiento, la inspiración y la búsqueda de sentido en el viaje de la vida nos guían para tomar la decisión más importante de todas: aquella que transforma nuestra propia realidad y la de quienes nos rodean.   Una invitación a pausar, introspeccionar y asumir con consciencia la dirección que le damos a nuestras vidas.   El Dr. Chandra Choubey es Director General del Tecnológico de Monterrey, Campus Toluca, académico, conferencista internacional y líder educativo con una desta

author: TEDx Talks
description: At eleven, Lidiia Reviakina moved from Ukraine to the United States and sat in classrooms pretending to laugh at jokes she didn’t understand. Years later, millions of Americans were laughing at hers. As creator Adil Revi (@adilrevi), she built a combined audience of over 2 million followers through comedy about Slavic family dynamics, traditions, and relationships. But why were people who didn’t grow up in her culture laughing too? She discovered that they saw their own families, relationships, and experiences in her stories. Her talk explores how humor became a bridge to belonging - and how laughter can help us recognize ourselves in each other long before we fully understand each other.  Lidiia Reviakina moved from the Ukraine to the United States when she was 12 years old. She struggled with English and began making videos about culture, relationships and social behavior as a digital content creator and observational comedian. She has connected with millions of people through humor
title: Before I Spoke the Language | Lidiia Reviakina | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description: From the stage to the clinic, decades of helping people who struggle with their voice and breathing have taught Claudio Milstein this: sometimes, something our bodies have done automatically for a lifetime can suddenly stop working. And yet, nothing appears to be damaged. So what has gone wrong? And can the body learn to work normally again? Dr. Claudio Milstein is an internationally recognized clinician, scientist, educator and speaker whose work has advanced the diagnosis and treatment of breathing and voice disorders. Born and trained in Buenos Aires, Argentina, he earned a doctorate in Speech Sciences before joining Cleveland Clinic. He has spent more than 25 years asking a simple question: Why do some people continue to suffer when no one can explain why? His innovative work first restored the voices of patients with previously unexplained voice disorders and later advanced care for people with unexplained breathing problems. Dr. Milstein is a full professor of Otolaryngology, au
title: The Mystery of Lost Voice and Breath | Claudio Milstein | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity

description: Safe spaces are lifelines for marginalized people that affirm identity, protect cultural difference, and build community, yet they shield institutions from accountability. When safety is confined to a single room, systems can appear progressive without confronting deeper inequities, making belonging conditional rather than structural. Richard Austin examines both the empowerment and the harm safe spaces can perpetuate, arguing that real inclusion demands a both-and approach: refuge and systemic redesign. True belonging requires transformation, not symbolism. Richard Austin is a scholar-practitioner in urban education, youth development leader and former professional athlete whose work focuses on educational equity, student belonging and leadership development. He serves as director of Ignatian and Community Belonging at St. Ignatius High School, where he leads initiatives that foster inclusive, mission-driven school communities. He earned a doctorate in urban education from Cleveland
title: Brand New Air | Richard Austin | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Objects can inspire a similar experience that explorers have when traversing the unknown. They can lead us to discover interesting, unexpected, and inspiring stories but it can take some practice to unlock their mysteries. Sabine Kretzschmar's talk draws on research from education and material cultural specialists as well as her own experience to describe how and why object-based learning can inspire learning for learning’s sake. With an open mind, a bit of imagination, and a willingness to follow your curiosity, the journey can be transformational. Sabine Kretzschmar is an art historian and museum professional with more than 30 years of experience as a curator, museum educator, collections director and university lecturer. As director of the Education Art Collection at the Cleveland Museum of Art, she oversees a teaching collection of more than 10,000 objects spanning 6,000 years of human history. 

A passionate advocate for object-based learning, Kretzschmar also partners with Cleve
title: Grab their Attention with Things of this World | Sabine Kretzschmar | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description: Songs do more than entertain; they preserve history. Charlie Mosbrook examines how music has documented human experiences across generations, giving voice to triumph, tragedy, and social change. Through examples from folk, blues, and contemporary music, he reveals why songs remain one of our most enduring tools for remembering the past and passing it along to the future. Charlie Mosbrook is an award-winning songwriter, vice president of Folk Alliance International and president of Folknet. He also serves as program and education director for Roots of American Music, advancing music education across Northeast Ohio. His songwriting has been recognized by the Woody Guthrie Folk Festival and John Hartford Memorial Festival, and he received the Folk Alliance Region Midwest Lantern Bearer Award in 2025. A longtime interpreter of Woody Guthrie's music, Mosbrook has performed at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and released *There Is a Better World Coming*, a tribute to Guthrie and the music of t
title: Understanding the human experience through song. | Charlie Mosbrook | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens when we approach cultural scripts with curiosity instead of judgement? Each of us carry cultural scripts that exist just beyond our awareness.  Stacey Litam shows us how once untangled, these beliefs can illuminate powerful opportunities to drive positive change and break generational trauma patterns. Stacey Diane Arañez Litam is an associate professor of counselor education at Cleveland State University, a licensed professional clinical counselor, clinical sexologist and racial equity strategist. A member of the Forbes Health Advisory Board, she also serves in national leadership roles with the National Board for Certified Counselors and on advisory boards for the Cleveland Clinic and the Philippine American Society of Ohio. Named to Crain's Cleveland Business' 40 Under 40 in 2023, Litam is a leading researcher on the effects of racial discrimination on mental health. Her work has been featured by the White House, NIH, NPR, Forbes Health and other national organizations
title: Breaking generational trauma patterns | Stacey Litam | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description: Water is so commonplace that most of us rarely stop to consider the innovation required to deliver it safely to our homes and communities. Samantha Martin explores how water has shaped the past, present, and future of Cleveland, Ohio. From fueling the city’s rise as an industrial powerhouse to becoming the catalyst for one of America’s most influential environmental movements following the Cuyahoga River fire, water has continuously driven transformation. Today, that same legacy is positioning the region as a global center for water technology and innovation. Through stories of environmental recovery, emerging technologies, and international collaboration, Samantha reveals how communities can turn historic challenges into opportunities for growth and impact. Ultimately, her talk invites audiences to see water not simply as a resource, but as a powerful force for innovation, resilience, and economic renewal. title: Turning Tides Burning River to Blue Tech | Samantha Martin | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity
